source.title: Memorization in Deep Neural Networks: Does the Loss Function Matter?

record.tranche_reason: The study’s own experiments refine the account of random-label memorization by showing that changing the loss function changes training-set fit; it does not measure held-out accuracy on natural labels.
record.gate_note: The paper reports random-label training accuracy and accuracy against the original labels of the same training examples. It does not report held-out test error on natural labels, so these results do not test the claim versions as written. Figure values are not numerically recoverable from the supplied text.
record.test_reason: The study measures fitting partially corrupted training labels and recovering original labels on those same training inputs. It does not measure held-out accuracy, so it does not test V1's coexistence of memorization and generalization. Its loss-function comparisons and population-risk argument do not test V2–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that changing the loss alone can substantially change memorization, demonstrate resistance with symmetric losses, and offer a theoretical explanation. They do not empirically establish held-out generalization.
record.recipe_differences: The study changes the loss function while otherwise keeping the training algorithm the same; it compares CCE, MSE, RLL and normalized MSE. It uses random-label training accuracy and accuracy against original training labels, not held-out test error on natural labels.
record.method_sensitivity: Loss function and label-noise rate change training-set fitting; the paper reports these across CIFAR-10 and MNIST architectures.

fits_no_version.finding: CCE and MSE generally achieve near-zero error on partially corrupted training labels; ResNet-18 with MSE is an exception. RLL resists fitting corrupted labels, and normalized MSE also produces incomplete fit.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Loss choice changes the extent to which the tested networks fit partially corrupted training labels.

fits_no_version.finding: With RLL at noise rates 0.2 and 0.4, accuracy against original training labels remains close to clean-data training accuracy. The population-risk theorem preserves risk rankings under symmetric label noise below (K−1)/K.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Symmetric losses can preserve original-label learning under partial symmetric label corruption; the empirical evidence concerns training inputs, and the theorem concerns population risk.

record.peer_reviewed: Pacific-Asia Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining (PAKDD-2021)
record.problems: No held-out natural-label test result is reported. The empirical results are presented mainly in figures, and the supplied text gives qualitative descriptions rather than exact values or uncertainty estimates. The study tests a range of label-noise rates but not η=1.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 4 reports J1 and J2 curves for CCE, MSE and RLL, including comparisons against original labels on the same training examples. Those separate curves are not extracted as additional rows because the supplied text gives only qualitative comparisons, not values that can be assigned by condition. Figure 5 also shows training accuracy and J1/J2 curves for normalized MSE; only the textually described training-accuracy result is recorded.

untested.parts: Coexistence of near-perfect random-label fitting with above-chance held-out natural-label accuracy under the same recipe, and chance held-out accuracy with random labels. Only training-label corruption rates through 0.6 are tested.
Width beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected held-out performance and local connectivity.
Optimizer comparisons on held-out performance under comparable tuning.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Test-accuracy effects of removing memorized versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The qualitative training-fit findings are readable without exact figure values. The cannot_determine states concern their inability to establish any listed version. Figure 4 and the additional Figure 5 curves are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: The paper measures fitting randomized training labels, but does not measure held-out accuracy on natural labels or establish coexistence of random-label fitting with natural-label generalization.
No width sweep or test-error result.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks.
No comparison of adaptive optimizers with SGD on held-out performance.
